note: The British Indian Ocean Territory, read on 2026-10-30 in the judgment of the BIOT Supreme Court of 31 March 2026 in R (Mandarin) v HM BIOT Commissioner (on the BIOT Administration's own site), which quotes the British Indian Ocean Territory (Immigration) Order 2004, and on the Administration's pages (About; Visa requirements). No person may enter or be present in the Territory without a permit issued under section 7 of the Order (members of the armed forces and public officers on duty excepted); an immigration officer issues or renews one in his entire discretion; a permit lasts four years from issue or a shorter period stated in it (term: four years, the longest; renewable). The permit isn't tied to a purpose in the Order, so it is written as a general route. The Constitution Order 2004's section 9 ('no person has the right of abode in the Territory') was quashed by the same judgment, which holds section 5 of the Immigration Order valid and asks future permit decisions to weigh the right of abode of any Chagossian entitled to it. About 2,000 people are ordinarily on Diego Garcia, mostly UK and US military, BIOTA officials and civilian contractors; there are no visa requirements, and visitors need prior approval. Not stated: a fee, a time, where it is applied for, the work it allows. The 2025 treaty with Mauritius was signed and its Bill not yet assented on the judgment's date.

sources.title: BIOT Supreme Court, R (Mandarin and others) v HM Commissioner for the British Indian Ocean Territory, judgment of 31 March 2026
sources.said: No person shall enter the Territory or be present there unless he is in possession of a permit issued under section 7 or his name is endorsed on a permit under section 9. ... An immigration officer, acting in his entire discretion, may issue or renew a permit or may cancel a permit before its expiration ... A permit shall, unless cancelled, remain in force for a period of four years from the date of issue or for such shorter period as is stated in it. ... I quash and will declare that Section 9 of the Constitutional Order 2004 is unlawful and/or Wednesbury unreasonable, especially in light of the current circumstances. ... Section 5 of the Immigration Order 2004 remains valid. ... Any future decisions of the Defendant in relation to the grant of permits need to take into account all the circumstances including heritage rights and the right of abode of any Chagossian entitled to them.

sources.title: British Indian Ocean Territory Administration, About
sources.said: There are ordinarily around 2000 people on Diego Garcia. They are mostly a mix of UK and US military personnel, BIOTA officials and civilian contractors responsible for the maintenance and operation of the military facility.

sources.title: British Indian Ocean Territory Administration, Visa requirements
sources.said: There are no visa requirements for BIOT. Those visiting the Territory must have prior approval.
